composio.note: Composio-managed OAuth is fine for prototyping, but the consent screen then shows Composio and you get Composio's default scopes; Composio's docs also note that managed apps share quota across Composio users (on GitHub, calls made with a user's token count against that user's 5,000 req/h regardless of which app makes them, while app-level limits such as 2,000 OAuth token requests/h are shared). Bring your own app when you want your product name on the GitHub authorization screen, fine-grained GitHub App permissions (e.g. contents read-only), a 15,000 req/h user-token limit (only if the app is owned by a GitHub Enterprise Cloud org), or polling faster than Composio's 15-minute managed minimum. If you bring a GitHub App, users must also install it on their account/org; Composio does not generate that installation link for you.

verdict.headline: Register a GitHub App (not an OAuth App), set it to 'Any account', paste its client ID/secret into Composio, and you can go live the same day with no GitHub review.
verdict.summary: GitHub has no app review: any GitHub App or OAuth App can be authorized by any user as soon as it exists. The friction is choosing correctly. GitHub recommends GitHub Apps (fine-grained permissions, per-repo install, expiring tokens, scaling rate limits), but they need a separate install step on each account/org. OAuth Apps are simpler but are blocked by OAuth app access restrictions, which are on by default for new organizations, so org data is invisible until an owner approves.
verdict.time_to_production: Same day; no provider review. Org customers may add their own owner-approval delay.
verdict.hands_on_effort: About 1 hour including testing token refresh (estimate)
verdict.approval_wait: None from GitHub. Inside customer organizations, an org owner must approve a GitHub App's organization permissions (and OAuth Apps when access restrictions are on). Marketplace listing is optional.

phases.name: Choose app type and register
phases.goal: A GitHub App exists with the right permissions, callback URL and installability.

steps.title: Pick GitHub App over OAuth App
steps.detail: For an AI agent, use a GitHub App: users choose which repositories it can reach, permissions are granular (e.g. read code without issues), user tokens expire after 8 hours, it is not subject to org OAuth app policies, and installation rate limits scale up to 12,500 req/h. Choose an OAuth App only if you need enterprise-level resources, which GitHub Apps cannot be granted yet.
steps.agent_help: Agent can map your agent's tools (read repo, open PRs, comment on issues) to the minimal GitHub App permissions and write the decision down.

steps.title: Register the GitHub App
steps.detail: At Settings > Developer settings > GitHub Apps > New GitHub App: set a name and homepage; add up to 10 Callback URLs; keep 'Expire user authorization tokens' checked; optionally check 'Request user authorization (OAuth) during installation'; uncheck Webhook 'Active' if you don't need events (webhook URL is then not required); set each permission to No access / Read-only / Read & write; under 'Where can this GitHub App be installed?' choose 'Any account' for a multi-customer product.
steps.agent_help: Agent prepares the exact field values (name, callback URL, permission matrix) as a checklist; you log in (2FA) and fill the form.

steps.title: Copy client ID and generate a client secret
steps.detail: From the app's settings page copy the Client ID and generate a Client Secret; you will paste both into Composio. Store the secret in a secret manager, never in source.

phases.name: Connect to Composio
phases.goal: Composio uses your GitHub App instead of its managed one.

steps.title: Create a custom auth config
steps.detail: Composio dashboard > Auth Configs > Create Auth Config > GitHub > OAuth2; paste Client ID and Client Secret; create and copy the ac_... id. Pass it per session, e.g. composio.create(user_id=..., auth_configs={"github": "ac_..."}). Toolkits you omit keep using managed auth.
steps.agent_help: Agent can write the session code with the auth_configs mapping; you paste the secret into the dashboard.

steps.title: Register Composio's redirect URI as a Callback URL
steps.detail: Add https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback to the GitHub App's Callback URLs. Some Composio toolkits still default to the legacy https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add, so copy the exact URI the Composio dashboard shows for your auth config. GitHub requires redirect_uri to match a registered callback URL and to carry no extra parameters.
steps.agent_help: Agent can compare the URI shown in the Composio dashboard with the GitHub App's callback list and flag any mismatch.

steps.title: Give users an installation link
steps.detail: With a GitHub App, OAuth authorization and installation are separate. Users must install the app on their account/org and pick repositories (https://github.com/apps/<your-app-slug>/installations/new). Composio does not generate this link, so surface it in your onboarding. A user token only reaches repositories that both the user and the app installation can access.
steps.agent_help: Agent can add an 'Install on GitHub' button and a post-connect check that lists accessible repos and prompts the install if none come back.

phases.name: Test with your own account
phases.goal: Your own account connects, calls the API and survives a token refresh.

steps.title: Install and authorize on your account
steps.detail: Install the app on your personal account or a test org, then run the Composio connect flow. Confirm the consent screen shows your app name and the requested permissions.
steps.agent_help: Agent can generate the Composio connect link and then call a read endpoint (list repos) to verify access.

steps.title: Verify token expiry and refresh
steps.detail: User access tokens expire after 8 hours (expires_in 28800); refresh tokens after 6 months. Refreshing returns a new access token and a new refresh token and invalidates the old pair, so serialize refreshes per user. If the refresh token is expired or reused you get bad_refresh_token and the user must re-authorize.
steps.agent_help: Agent can force a refresh via POST https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token with grant_type=refresh_token and confirm the stored token was replaced.

phases.name: Launch
phases.goal: Any GitHub user or organization can install and connect.
phases.duration: Same day (plus each customer org's own approval)

steps.title: Make sure the app is public
steps.detail: If you registered it as 'Only on this account', switch it to public so any GitHub user can install it. GitHub documents no review for this.

steps.title: Expect org-owner approval at customers
steps.detail: Installing on an organization needs an org owner or repo admin, and an owner must approve any organization permissions. Tell enterprise customers this up front.
steps.agent_help: Agent can draft a one-paragraph 'what we access and why' note for customer admins.

steps.title: Optional: list on GitHub Marketplace
steps.detail: Public apps get an install landing page automatically. Marketplace listing is optional and only for distribution and discovery.
steps.agent_help: Agent can draft listing copy; you submit it.

requirements.item: GitHub personal or organization account to own the app
requirements.detail: An account or organization can register up to 100 GitHub Apps.
Up to 10 per GitHub App. redirect_uri must match one of them and can't carry extra parameters; if omitted, GitHub uses the first.

requirements.item: Webhook URL (only if webhooks are Active)
requirements.detail: Uncheck 'Active' if the agent doesn't consume events; a webhook secret is highly recommended when active.
Required so users outside your account can install the app.
Optional; only public apps can publish to GitHub Marketplace.

scopes.scope: GitHub App permission: Repository contents (Read & write)
scopes.purpose: Read code and push commits/branches for the agent.
scopes.review_impact: No GitHub review. User picks which repos the installation can reach; prefer Read-only if the agent doesn't write.

scopes.scope: GitHub App permissions: Issues and Pull requests (Read & write)
scopes.purpose: Read/comment on issues, open and review PRs.
scopes.review_impact: No GitHub review; shown on the install/consent screen.

scopes.scope: GitHub App organization permissions (e.g. Members read)
scopes.review_impact: An org owner must approve organization permissions at install.

scopes.purpose: Alternative if you build an OAuth App: full access to the user's repos.
scopes.review_impact: No GitHub review, but very broad (code + issues + PRs on every repo the user can access); blocked for org data when OAuth app access restrictions are on (default for new orgs).

scopes.purpose: Forces an expiring token plus refresh token for one authorization even if the app hasn't opted in.
scopes.review_impact: None; not tracked as a regular scope and adds no prompt.

oauth.pkce: Supported: code_challenge with code_challenge_method=S256 only (plain not supported); code_verifier required at exchange if a challenge was sent. Strongly recommended for OAuth Apps.
oauth.refresh_tokens: GitHub App user tokens expire after 8 hours (expires_in 28800) by default with a refresh token valid 6 months (15897600 s). Each refresh returns a new access+refresh pair and invalidates the old ones (single-use). Expiry can be opted out per app (not recommended). OAuth App tokens are long-lived unless expiring tokens are enabled app-wide or offline_access is requested. Refresh cannot change scopes.
oauth.redirect_uri_rules: GitHub App: up to 10 callback URLs; redirect_uri must match one exactly and cannot add parameters; default is the first. OAuth App: exact match unless per-URL wildcard matching is on (host and port must match, path may be a subdirectory); apps that had a single callback URL before 3 Aug 2026 have wildcard matching enabled for it (GitHub recommends disabling it if not needed). Native apps should use 127.0.0.1 or ::1 loopback (port may differ), not 'localhost'.

limits.limit: User access tokens: 5,000 requests/hour, shared with the user's PATs and other OAuth apps
limits.applies_when: Agent calls the API as the user (Composio's default for user-connected accounts)
limits.how_to_lift: Use GitHub App installation tokens for bot-style work, or Enterprise Cloud orgs (15,000/h).

limits.limit: GitHub App installation: 5,000 req/h base, +50/h per repo and per org user beyond 20, capped at 12,500 (15,000 on Enterprise Cloud)
limits.how_to_lift: Scales automatically; not available to OAuth Apps.

limits.limit: Secondary limits: 100 concurrent requests; 900 points/min per REST endpoint; 80 content-creating requests/min and 500/h
limits.how_to_lift: GitHub documents no way to raise them; honor retry-after / x-ratelimit-reset on 403/429. Repeated violations can get the integration banned.
Cache tokens and refresh only near expiry.

blockers.symptom: GitHub shows a redirect_uri mismatch error instead of the consent screen.
blockers.fix: Add the exact Composio callback URI (v3 or legacy v1, whichever the dashboard shows) to the app's Callback URLs, with no query parameters.

blockers.symptom: Connection succeeds but list-repos returns nothing / 404 on org repos.
blockers.fix: Send the user to the app's installation page to install it and select repositories; tokens only reach repos both user and installation can access.

blockers.blocker: OAuth app access restrictions (OAuth Apps only)
blockers.symptom: User authorized your OAuth App but org repos are missing; the user can only 'request' access.
blockers.fix: Ask an org owner to approve the app, or switch to a GitHub App, which is not subject to these org policies.
Persist the new refresh token from every refresh, serialize refreshes per user; if expired (6 months unused) re-run the authorization flow.

agent_can: Decide GitHub App vs OAuth App and produce the minimal permission matrix
Prepare every registration field value (name, callback URLs, webhook off, 'Any account')
Write Composio session code with auth_configs={"github": "ac_..."}
Build the 'Install on GitHub' onboarding link and a post-connect repo-access check
Test token refresh and rate-limit handling (retry-after, serialized refresh)
you_must: Log in to GitHub (2FA) and submit the New GitHub App form
Generate and store the client secret, and paste it into the Composio dashboard
Install the app on your own account to test
Switch the app to public / 'Any account' when ready
